items.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001
items.q: there was this jazz party that this man Dick Gibson would give, at the Broadmoor.

ctx.x: You had a fortuitous meeting with Clark Terry somewhere early on, didn’t you?

Yes. I met Clark — our jazz band won a city wide competition which allowed us to go to Chicago and perform for what was then called the National Association of Jazz Educators. And of course Clark has been affiliated with them for a long time. And he heard me and we started talking, and I didn’t know who he was, I just knew he was this nice man. My uncle was, “That’s Clark Terry” you know. And it’s like okay. So when he would come to Denver, there was this jazz party that this man Dick Gibson would give, at the…

Rowles. It was pretty amazing. Eddie “Lockjaw” Davis. And I would come there with all my music together. My uncle would help me get it together, my keys, and tell them how I wanted to do these little head arrangements, because I was really into that and Clark just stayed in touch. And from that point on we just continued to work together and we still do.
